body.p: Claims 1-10, 13, 14, and 16-23 are pending, with claims 1, 9, and 13 being independent. Claim 1 is amended, support for which can be found, for example, in claim 5 and paragraph [00106] of the specification; and corresponding amendments are made to claims 9 and 13. Claims 5 and 21 are canceled. Claims 2, 3, 18, and 19 are amended to adapt to the amendments to claim 1. No new matter is added.
In the Office Action, claims 1, 9, and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as

being anticipated by U.S. Pub. No. 2020/0026421 (Rosa); claims 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 14, and 16-23 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Rosa in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2014/0309879 (Ricci); and claims 2 and 6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Rosa in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0324527 (Presant). The rejections are respectfully overcome by amendment, in view of the following remarks.
Amended claim 1 recites, in relevant part:

wherein a recommended gesture corresponding to each sub- function is stored in the vehicle; and when the recommended gesture corresponding to each sub-function in the target function is a periodic gesture, wherein the periodic gesture indicates that a driver needs to periodically execute a gesture operation to control the vehicle to continuously execute the target function, the step of, when the current gesture data meets the preset condition, generating the target control instruction according to the current gesture data, and sending the target control instruction to the target
executive mechanism, comprises:
determining expected gesture data according to the gesture data acquired last time and the recommended gesture
corresponding to each sub-function in the target function; and

if a difference value between the current gesture data and the expected gesture data is within a third preset range, generating the target control instruction according to the current gesture data, and sending the target control instruction to the target executive
mechanism.

Corresponding features can be found in amended claims 9 and 13. The Office Action argues that the combination of Rosa and Ricci teaches the features originally recited in claim 5. See Office Action at p. 4-5. Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of cited references fails to teach these features, as now recited in amended claim 1.

Rosa provides an input device, such as for a vehicle, whereby a gesture may be provided to present an application associated with the gesture, even if another application is being displayed by an output. If a gesture does not match, the gesture may be processed as an input to the other application currently displayed. A time shift algorithm may be utilized to determine if the received gesture matches the gesture associated with the other application. Additionally, a dedicated close gesture may be utilized to dismiss a currently displayed application.

As admitted in the Office Action, Rosa fails to disclose gestures directed to sub-functions or mapping to a preset function or determining when a prior gesture was input the last time. See Office Action at p. 4. In addition, while Rosa discloses a gesture in paragraphs [0130]-[0134] and [0138], Rosa fails to disclose that "a recommended gesture corresponding to each sub- function in the target function is a periodic gesture," and that "the periodic gesture indicates that a driver needs to periodically execute a gesture operation to control the vehicle to continuously execute the target function," as required by amended claim 1. Consequently, Rosa also fails to disclose "determining expected gesture data according to the gesture data acquired last time and the recommended gesture corresponding to each sub-function in the target function," as required by amended claim 1.

Ricci discloses in paragraph [0502] that "the origin module 2008 is generally operable to determine the origin of a gesture. The origin of the gesture may be the same as the location of the person providing the gesture, or may be a different zone 512, a different area 508, a different location within a zone 512 or area 508, or on a console 248 that is near the person." However, Ricci only discloses the location of the gesture, and Ricci also fails to disclose the specific gesture type.
In contrast, the gesture of amended claim 1 is a "periodic gesture," and the periodic gesture indicates that a driver needs to periodically execute a gesture operation to control the Page 12 of 14

vehicle to continuously execute the target function. Ricci fails to disclose a "periodic gesture" and also fails to teach that "the periodic gesture indicates that a driver needs to periodically execute a gesture operation to control the vehicle to continuously execute the target function," as required by amended claim 1. Consequently, Ricci also fails to disclose "determining expected gesture data according to the gesture data acquired last time and the recommended gesture corresponding to each sub-function in the target function," as required by amended claim 1. Thus, Ricci fails to make up for the deficiencies of Rosa.
Presant fails to make up for the deficiencies of Rosa and Ricci. Thus, amended claim 1 is believed to be patentable over the cited references.

Amended claims 9 and 13 recite similar features to those of amended claim 1 described above. Thus, amended claims 9 and 13 are believed to be patentable over the cited references for the same reasons provided above.

Claims 2-4, 6-8, 14, 16-20, 22, and 23 depend from amended claims 1 and 9 and inherit all limitations thereof. Thus, claims 2-4, 6-8, 14, 16-20, 22, and 23 are believed to be patentable over the cited references at least for the reasons provided above.
Claims 5 and 21 are canceled, rendering the rejections of these claims moot.
In view of the above, removal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103 is respectfully requested.

It is respectfully submitted that a full and complete response to the Office Action has been made. Favorable reconsideration of the application is kindly sought. If the Examiner has any further questions or concerns, the Examiner is invited to contact the Applicant's undersigned practitioner.
The Applicant believes that no extension-of-time is needed in order to enter this
Response. However, if an extension-of-time is needed, please consider this to be a petition for
